headline: Nairobi's Libraries Rise From Neglect to Become Free Study Hubs
meta_description: Book Bunk nonprofit transforms Nairobi's crumbling public libraries into thriving civic spaces, serving 192,000 users and creating 93 jobs.
summary_short: Nairobi's abandoned libraries are becoming vibrant community hubs. One organization has already transformed three branches and served 140,000 free meals.
body:
When Sunil Totti needed a reliable place to prepare for a tech job interview, he found refuge at Eastlands Library—a space he once avoided as a dusty, neglected building. Today, the 26-year-old spends eight or nine hours there most days, using its free computers and internet to study software development and fintech. His story reflects a quiet revolution unfolding across Nairobi: the nonprofit Book Bunk has rescued three of the city's public libraries from decay, transforming them into free civic hubs where thousands now work, study, and learn. The results speak clearly—patronage has risen by more than 240 percent, with over 192,000 direct users and 45,000 participants in free education programs.

Founded in 2017 by writer Wanjiru Koinange and publisher Angela Wachuka, Book Bunk discovered its mission almost by accident. While searching for a venue for a literary festival at McMillan Memorial—Nairobi's oldest library, opened in 1931—the pair found crumbling walls, flooded basements, and rotting books. That discovery led them to the other two branches in similar condition. Rather than simply refurbishing shelves, Book Bunk reimagined these spaces entirely. The organization has served over 140,000 free meals to remove barriers to attendance, catalogued 138,000 books, and added 23,000 titles emphasizing African authors. The work has created 93 jobs and engaged 400 local vendors.

Yet challenges remain. School holiday programs overflow—600 children apply for 200 available spots at Eastlands. The partnership between the city council and Book Bunk, while creative, depends on donor funding and shifting political relationships. As one observer notes, civil society cannot permanently substitute for government responsibility. Still, Book Bunk's Blueprint is being mapped for scale across Kenya's 1,196 public libraries, with potential for replication in fast-growing cities across the Global South.
quick_facts: Book Bunk transformed three Nairobi libraries since 2017
Over 140,000 free meals served to remove attendance barriers
23,000 new titles added, emphasizing African authors
